part.text:
The client is pushing back via chat. I need to respond as the preparer — explain the Form 7203 basis limitation with the arithmetic and library authority, why Pike's guarantee doesn't create debt basis, why buddy's CPA situation may differ (more basis, prior loans, income, later years), and what could fix it (capital contribution, shareholder loan). Don't change numbers. Flag: this is the client arguing; our figures stand. Update judgment_calls.md? The contract says judgment_calls.md should capture every decision. The basis decision is already documented (item 1). I could add a note about the client challenge and the alternative (guarantee → no debt basis) which is already there. Maybe add explicit note in judgment_calls item 1 that the client was informed and the position is maintained. Also possibly STATUS unchanged. Maybe update QUESTIONS.md? No — no new facts needed.

Key points to explain carefully with numbers:
- Basis walk: 10,000 contribution → losses/income/distributions in order → 11,500 at 1/1/2025.
- 2023 and 2024 distributions already took basis down: 12,000 + 5,200 = 17,200 of past cash out reduced the cushion.
- Loss 28,000 > 11,500 → allowed 11,500, suspended 16,500 carried forward [3].
- Guarantee doesn't create debt basis [3]: need actual loan from Marcus to the corporation.
- Buddy's CPA scenario: his friend's basis may have been higher, the friend may have lent the company money, his loss may have been smaller, or the CPA simply used income later — we can't know; also possible the CPA is wrong or made basis restorations. Our arithmetic: even the friend's identity as shareholder of the same company? No — different company (his buddy — is it also Reyes & Pike? "My buddy's CPA" — the buddy might be Pike? No, his buddy is a different person). Different company, different basis.
- Suspended carries forward: 16,500 not lost; restores as income/basis builds; also future K-1 income or contributions add basis.
- If Marcus wants to use it now: he could have lent money to the S-corp in 2025 (not guarantee); new basis from contributions can't be applied retroactively. Actually — a loan made in 2025 would create debt basis prospectively; cannot help 2025 already ended? We don't invent facts; the file says he never lent money. We can note for the future.
- Also note the excess loss reduces MAGI for 8582 only to the extent allowed — we did that.

Where to record: The deliverable set should stay accurate. I'll:
1. Reply to the client in chat with the explanation (concise, readable, with arithmetic).
2. Add a note to judgment_calls.md item 1 documenting the client challenge and why the guarantee alternative is rejected (already states no debt basis) — append "Client challenged 12/2025 season: position confirmed; explanation provided" plus numbers.
3. No numeric changes; STATUS.md — maybe append a line noting the challenge was addressed and no change. Keep small.

Let me do the file updates briefly, then answer. The chat reply tone: professional, direct, cite library only.

Recomputing the basis walk to present cleanly:
- 2021: +10,000 − 2,100 → 7,900
- 2022: +6,400 → 14,300
- 2023: +9,800 → 24,100, then −12,000 distribution → 12,100 (order per [3]: income first, then distributions)
- 2024: +4,600 → 16,700, −5,200 → 11,500
- 2025: available 11,500 vs 28,000 loss → 11,500 allowed, 16,500 suspended.

Also distributions came IN CASH to him — that's why cushion shrank: he took out 17,200 while income added 20,800 & loss removed 2,100. Net effect 10,000 + 20,800 − 2,100 − 17,200 = 11,500. Good framing: "you didn't leave the cushion in the company."

The friend comparison possibilities: (1) buddy contributed/lent money or had no distributions → more basis; (2) buddy's s-corp loss smaller; (3) the CPA might figure basis from the wrong records; (4) some CPAs get this wrong. I should not accuse; just say I can't see his friend's file; our facts: no shareholder loans, guarantee only; the library explicitly says guarantee ≠ debt basis.

Also mention: if the corporation had borrowed from Marcus personally (direct loan), debt basis would exist — it didn't happen per his own note; and Pike guaranteeing ≠ Marcus loaning even though Pike is his partner.

Also could a 2025 contribution fix 2025? Only if made/gifted before the return is filed? No — basis is determined as of the close of the taxable year; a contribution during 2025 adds basis for 2025; a contribution in 2026 does NOT (for 2025). Don't suggest advice beyond; can note 16,500 suspends and will free up with 2026 income or new contributions/loans made in a future year. Also note: the withheld-return implication: allowed 11,500 already saves at 24%-ish? We don't have rate schedules beyond; keep it qualitative-ish, cite that the loss DOES reduce AGI by 11,500 already plus MAGI effects. Maybe just say: "the 11,500 allowed already drops AGI by 11,500 (and raises your 8582 allowance by up to 5,750 via MAGI reduction — 50% of 11,500)". Actually MAGI effect: allowance = 25,000 − 50%×(MAGI−100,000); allowing 11,500 raises allowance by 5,750. Nice point: the allowed portion is doing double duty already.

Keep reply tight: explanation + why not guarantee + what would create debt basis + what happens to 16,500 + note friend's facts unknown. Also update judgment_calls.md + STATUS.md one line each.

File edits:
- judgment_calls.md item 1: append client-challenge sentence.
- STATUS.md: add note in "Open items" or a new line "Client challenge re basis addressed 2026?; no change." Keep one line.
安静的时间 — 此问题无需文件编辑；数值依然成立。客户端正在争辩已显示的数字。我直接回答并附上计算过程，然后否决该担保方案，最后记录下已对该挑战进行审查。

part.text: Now the reply to Marcus. Format: short, arithmetic walk table, why the guarantee fails, why friend's case may differ, where the 16,500 goes. Keep concise.

Marcus, I get why it feels arbitrary — here's the walk, and your buddy's deal almost certainly isn't the same shape as yours.

**Your basis at January 1, 2025 = $11,500.** Form 7203 makes you add up every dollar you left in the company and take out every dollar it paid you (Form 7203 instructions, library §3 — income first, then distributions):

| Year | Started | K-1 income/(loss) | Distributions | Ended |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2021 | 10,000 contribution | (2,100) | 0 | 7,900 |
| 2022 | 7,900 | 6,400 | 0 | 14,300 |
| 2023 | 14,300 | 9,800 | (12,000) | 12,100 |
| 2024 | 12,100 | 4,600 | (5,200) | 11,500 |

The 2025 loss is **$28,000**, and a shareholder's loss is allowed "only to the extent of adjusted stock basis plus debt basis" — you had $11,500. So $11,500 is deducted now; **$16,500 suspends and carries forward indefinitely** until basis is restored. It is not lost — 2026 income, a fresh capital contribution, or an actual loan *from you* would start releasing it.

**Why not Pike's guarantee.** The Form 7203 instructions in our library are explicit: "A guarantee of corporate debt does **not** create debt basis; only a direct loan **from the shareholder** to the corporation does." Pike pledged his own credit to the bank; no money of yours went into the company, so there's nothing to hang a basis on. Your own note says you never lent the company money.

**Why your buddy could take his whole loss.** I can't see his file, but the likely differences: he had more basis entering the loss year — he never took distributions (you took out $17,200 in 2023–24, precisely what eroded your cushion), he has shareholder loans on the books, or his loss was smaller than his basis. One of those facts will be true for him and is false for you; the same $16,500-of-loss-over-$11,500-of-basis math applies to every shareholder, or his preparer simply carried basis wrong.

**One consolation already priced in:** the $11,500 allowed is doing maximum work — it cuts AGI dollar-for-dollar, and because it's a nonpassive loss, it also pulled your MAGI down $11,500, which *raised* your rental special allowance by $5,750 on Form 8582. The return.json figures stand: loss_allowed 11,500, loss_suspended 16,500. If you can get me 2025 documentation of a shareholder note to the company that your note didn't mention, I'll revisit — that's the only fact that could change this answer.
